accepted.sentence: In a concert band, it usually belongs to the low-brass section, where parts may support harmonies or answer melodic phrases.
Big-band charts often assign the instrument harmonized riffs and rhythmic accents behind a featured soloist.
In brass quintet writing, its middle-register line can connect higher brass parts with the tuba’s bass foundation.
Marching-band arrangements use its bold, projecting sound for melodic calls and rhythmic figures that remain audible outdoors.
New Orleans second-line parades often include it among the brass voices carrying layered melodies over a steady street beat.
In musical-theater pit orchestras, its parts may shift among lyrical lines, rhythmic accents, and sustained ensemble support as scenes change.
A choir made entirely of this instrument can range from bass foundations to high melodic lines, producing a unified brass texture.
In recording studios, engineers may place a microphone near its bell for direct sound, then adjust distance to blend room ambience.
